paragraphs: Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah: Mishnah, end of Eruvin, chapter 1, 16b; Sotah 9:9. He disputes with his father, the unqualified Rabbi Yehudah, bar Ilai; see Rashi there. Pesachim 4:6, 55a; Bava Metzia 7:3; Sanhedrin 8:3; Makkot, chapter 2, mishnayot 3 and 6, and 9b; Chullin 1:3, 18a; Zevachim 6:1; Menachot, end of chapter 8, mishnah 7, page 63 as cited. See 87a; Bekhorot 9:7; Temurah 2:3; Nedarim 8:6, 62a; Gittin 4:7. He disputes with his father in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Eruvin, chapter 1. He traveled with Rabbi, and they saw a gentile: Bereshit Rabbah, section 76. He commanded Rabbi three things: Arvei Pesachim 112b. He disputes with Rabbi: Sukkah 50b and end of Temurah. Sifrei, Haazinu, the section ‘He told them, Set your hearts’: Rabbenu came from Laodicea; Rabbi Y. entered from Laodicea; Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah entered. And Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Yehudah. At Yuchasin’s end, Yemot Olam, chapter 18: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, sons of Rabbi Yehudah, his colleague, his teacher. Eruvin 38b: Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah Setimaai; Rashi explains that he so calls anyone whose words Rabbi accepted in many places and taught anonymously. Bekhorot 51a as cited. See 51b: see Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon. In Rabbi Eliezer’s name: Pesachim 94b and Sotah 2b. Tosefta, beginning of Sotah, chapter 1, and Negaim, chapter 6: in Rabbi Elazar’s name. With Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon, they say: Shabbat 136a, Kiddushin 76, Nedarim 76b. Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah says; Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef said; Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya said: Yoma 85b. In Rabbi Zekharyah ben HaKatzav’s name. He spoke to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah and disputes with Rabbi Yaakov: end of Beitzah, chapter 4, 35b. End of Yoma, Shabbat 121a, and Makkot 6b raise a contradiction between Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Yose and answer: that is Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah. Rashi explains: this one is Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta. Tosafot, Yoma 8a, write that the reason it does not answer ‘That is Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah’ is because Rabbi Meir disputes with him; we infer that it is Rabbi Yose bar Chalafta. End quotation. Thus, although it says simply Rabbi Yose, we may say it is Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah. See Orach Mishor, Nazir 66, and above, Isi ben Akiva. ‘Rabbi Akiva’s words; Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah says,’ and so forth; ‘Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said’: Tosefta, final chapter of Bekhorot.
